description: One Svelte 5 data grid, one array of rows, and four renderers behind a switch: the plain table with inline editing, a Gantt chart with phases and dependency links, a resource timeline with a lane per owner, and a Kanban board of status lanes. Each view is the same SvGrid with a different prop (gantt, scheduler, board) and writes back through a callback to the same rows. Change a status in the table and the card moves lane; drag a bar in the Gantt and the timeline follows; drop a card on Done and its progress reads 100.

faq.question: Is it four components or one?
faq.answer: One. Each view is the same SvGrid with a different prop: gantt, scheduler or board. Without any of them it renders the table. The rows, columns and getRowId are shared, so the views cannot drift apart.

faq.question: How do edits in one view reach the others?
faq.answer: Every view reports what it wants through a callback (onTaskMove, onEventMove, onCardMove, onCellValueChange) and never mutates a row itself. The demo writes the change to the one rows array, and whichever view is showing reads it from there.

faq.question: Why are the dates stored as local timestamps?
faq.answer: So every view reads them the same way. A date-only string is a calendar day to the Gantt and UTC midnight to the scheduler, which west of Greenwich is the day before. A local timestamp with an exclusive end is unambiguous to all four.
